parts.part: fortified settlement (Area A: town wall with a north-western corner bastion)
parts.layout_phase: Period II (Mature Harappan); the excavators attribute the fortification to the arrival of the Harappans after a thin transitional phase, without tying it to one of the three Mature Harappan stages
parts.what_was_built: The first season (2012-13) exposed in Area A 'a ... massive wall of nearly 22.03m in length and 6.54m in thickness with two courses of large sized mud-bricks not confirming to any ratio', dividing the area into a richer southern part and a northern part with two house complexes; Period II houses used 8 x 16 x 32 cm bricks (1:2:4), the Early Harappan Period I houses 14 x 28 x 42 cm (1:2:3) (IAR 2012-13 p. 130). The second season re-opened these trenches and found 'a 6 m wide fortification wall ... with a northwest corner bastion', whose northern and western arms could be traced for 30 m each; it survives to three courses, rests 'on a 10 cm thick burnt layer' and was built in at least five portions of differently coloured bricks (IAR 2013-14 p. 105). The excavators link it to the Harappan arrival: the Area F remains indicate 'occupation of this area just prior to the mature Harappan phase and the arrival of Harappan might have prompted modification of the nature of settlement with the addition of fortifications, one portion of which could be traced in area A' (p. 108). A large-scale conflagration had ended the Early Harappan occupation (p. 89), and the excavators estimate that 'at least 70% of the fortified settlement was destroyed' by recent levelling (p. 86).
parts.excavator_basis: The IAR reports give no date range beyond placing the river and its settlements in 'the third millennium BCE' (IAR 2013-14 p. 84) and refer the dating to cultural affinities (Sothi-Siswal Period I, Mature Harappan Period II, seal bosses without bipartite division assigned to the early Mature Harappan, pp. 114, 117); no radiocarbon result is reported. The excavators' preliminary paper (Prabhakar and Majid 2014) was not obtained.

syntheses.statement: The Harappa.com summary of Prabhakar and Majid's preliminary report says the site 'has nevertheless yielded an impressive set of artifacts from about 2800-2000 BCE' and that the thin transitional phase to the Mature Harappan 'includes complete houses, a 6 meter wide mud-brick wall'.
syntheses.disagreement: The summary places the wall in the transitional phase, whereas IAR 2013-14 (p. 108) ties the fortification to the Harappan arrival; it does not say on what basis the 2800-2000 BCE span rests.

parts.conflicts: Whether the wall belongs to the transitional phase (Harappa.com summary) or to the Mature Harappan Period II (IAR 2013-14 p. 108) is not settled in the sources we read; neither gives a stratigraphic link between the wall and the three Mature Harappan stages of trench S170E40 III (IAR 2013-14 pp. 102-105).

parts.part: Area E street and house-blocks (north-east of Area A)
parts.layout_phase: Harappan phase (transitional and Mature Harappan); the street existed through at least five structural phases
parts.what_was_built: In Area E the excavators found 'Harappan phase occupation in the form of structural activities of at least five phases along a ... street of 2.5m in width', with house complexes on both edges and at least four phases of repair to the wall fronting the street, concluding that 'proper planning and layout were made for the occupation'; natural soil lay at 3.7 m in S30E130 (IAR 2013-14 p. 107), a deposit that 'corresponds to both transitional phase and mature Harappan period' (p. 87). The first season had reached natural soil at 1.9 m in two trenches here and found Mature Harappan occupation with two structural phases (IAR 2012-13 p. 133).
parts.excavator_basis: As for Area A: no date range or radiocarbon result in the IAR reports.
parts.conflicts: None found; the part rests on a single season's summary.

first_occupation.phase: Period I (Early Harappan, Sothi-Siswal ceramic complex), in Areas A, B and D; at least four structural phases in Area B and five stages in trench S170E40 III, ended by a large-scale conflagration
first_occupation.basis: Cultural attribution only; no radiocarbon result is reported in the IAR summaries. In S170E40 III the Early Harappan deposit is 2.53 m thick under 1.50 m of Mature Harappan deposit (IAR 2013-14 p. 87).

N. Prabhakar and Jaseera C. Majid's report of that title (Man and Environment 39(2), 2014, according to a search-engine record; the paper itself was not obtained).

notes: Karanpura, near Bhadra in Hanumangarh district on the dry Chautang (Drishadvati), was excavated by the ASI's Excavation Branch II in 2012-13 and 2013-14 under V. N. Prabhakar. The two IAR summaries give two periods, Early Harappan (I) and Mature Harappan (II), with a thin transitional phase between them, a Harappan fortification in Area A and a planned street in Area E. Most of the site was levelled for irrigation before excavation. No radiocarbon determination, date range or Bayesian model has been published in the sources we could open; the excavators' preliminary paper (Prabhakar and Majid, 'Preliminary Results of Excavation at Karanpura, a Harappan Settlement in District Hanumangarh, Rajasthan', said to be in Man and Environment 39(2), 2014) is behind an academia.edu login, the IIT Gandhinagar repository record could not be reached, and archive.org holds no Man and Environment volume after 36. The 2800-2000 BCE span is taken only from the Harappa.com summary of that paper. Orientation statements in the IAR text are omitted here.
